In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the functional response is a function of both predator size and the context in which it is operating, and that this context dependence can be quantified and predicted.
the functional responses of predators and their prey are not only size dependent but also dependent on the complexity and the dimension of the habitat in which they interact.
the scaling of feeding rates is context-dependent, and that the context of feeding can have profound consequences for the structure of food webs and the persistence of populations.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
context (habitat structure) can mediate consumer resource interactions.
context dependent scaling of feeding interactions is a potentially widespread phenomenon that may be a key factor in determining the dynamics of many consumer resource systems.
the context of consumer resource systems, in particular, the habitat structure, can have a strong effect on the scaling of feeding interactions.
The main takeaway from our work is that
consumer resource interactions can be highly sensitive to context.
consumer resource interactions can change with context, and thus we should not assume that the form of interactions remains constant across contexts.
consumer resource systems may be more stable than expected because interactions are not as strong as previously thought, particularly when prey are abundant.
